items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Sometime I'd go to Bonnie's house and we'd play in the backyard band. Next day maybe Bonnie would come to my house, same way with Danny.

ctx.x: What happened on the sidewalks then? You talk about your backyard. Did the kids play on the sidewalks?

Well, the little sidewalks that we had, yes. But mostly we could find ourselves playing in each other's yard. Sometime I'd go to Bonnie's house and we'd play in the backyard band. Next day maybe Bonnie would come to my house, same way with Danny. And then that night we'd go to picture shows, neighborhood theaters. We had the Ivy Theater right down the corner of Hillary. And then that, and we'd find decent pleasurable things to do. Not too much like, of course I don't want to condemn the error because in so doing…
Well I don't think all change is progress. I mean there's such a thing as progress and there's such a thing as just plain change. Something's good and something's bad.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: that's how Bonnie and I are cousins because my grandmother and his mother were sisters

ctx.x: And her first name? George Henry. George Anna Wright, I thought, see. And then the Begards and the Pirones are on, and I can't keep it all straight. Well, no,

I told you that was going to be complicated. The Begards are on the McKenna side. Bonnie's mother was my grandmother's sister. There were five sisters and about four or five brothers. So, after the sisters married, you have the Marqueses that come in there. That's another sister. So, it would take us two, three months to sit down here and go through each individual's married life and their offspring. But that's how Bonnie and I are cousins because my grandmother and his mother were sisters. And Bonnie was born, I…
know Emil, his father? Emil, the girl?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Well, my cousin, Bonnie Big, who's now with Louis Armstrong, he and I came up together almost like brothers.

ctx.x: I know Natty said he was raised that way.

On French, that's right. And I still talk French now. And then when someone, when I can talk with someone. So the first lesson I had at Nelson Jean's house, he was a great friend of the family, but he liked to take a drink of wine. So I went on my first lesson. And then, while he told me to get, had an old cornet that I bought somewhere. I don't know where it was. And anyhow, my daddy found it for me, I believe. And I was too young to remember. He wanted me to learn how to clean the horn. So I decided to clean…
We talked to one of the brothers of the old men. There was an old Lorenzo and a Louis Teo, Papa Teo.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Well, through Bonnie. Through Bonnie Biggore, my cousin. When they booked the tour in Texas, I wired Bonnie that I was there and I wanted them to be my guests at my house.

ctx.x: What about Duke Ellington? You know him personally?

Well sure. Duke and I are great friends. How'd that happen? Well, through Bonnie. Through Bonnie Biggore, my cousin. When they booked the tour in Texas, I wired Bonnie that I was there and I wanted them to be my guests at my house. So I met them in Austin, Texas, which is 75 miles from San Antonio and then I brought them into San Antonio. By the same token, cab the same way. In those days they had what they called the circuit where they played all of these theater dates. That's most of the dates that Ellington…
When did they have that flood there?
